scope: Proposition 6.5 (Low-density cones) of the manuscript “The Solomon–Yau least-volume theorem” (preprints/The-Solomon-Yau-least-volume-theorem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 349 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b44def9b041e8f31), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 28. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix m ≥ 2 and assume Theorem 1.1 in dimensions 2, . . . , m − 1, with an empty assumption when m = 2. Let C be a nonzero stationary integral k-dimensional cone in Rk+1 such that Θ(C, 0) < ϑm. (6.5) When m = 2 or m = 3, also assume that C is cyclic modulo two. Then: (i) if 1 ≤ k ≤ m, C is a multiplicity-one hyperplane; (ii) if k = m + 1, C is smooth embedded with multiplicity one away from its vertex. Its link in Sm+1 is a smooth closed connected embedded minimal hypersurface.
